IndyGuitarist Wampler Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by type simulation amp simulation browse by enclosure pedal Wampler Pedals cataPulp - British Distortion Published on September 1, 2015 Wampler Pedals amp simulation distortion pedal Information Wampler Pedals Several months ago Brian was approached to design a pedal that could faithfully reproduce the tones of a specific citrus colored, British amp made famous by artists like Jimmy Page, Weezer, Queens of the Stone Age, and Slipknot. After spending countless hours tweaking the circuit and testing it against those iconic amps - he did it! Introducing - the cataPulp. The cataPulp's gain structure truly represents what every great amp in a box (AIAB) should be - with super clean tones that get increasingly dirtier after the "12 o'clock" setting. This allows you to cover a lot of ground between those classic rock inspired tones all the way to a thick syrupy metal territory - Use it as a tone shaper or a secondary gain stage - a truly versatile tonal workhorse! The cataPulp also features an active 3 band EQ and top mounted jacks and our soft click electrical relay true by-pass switch. We use a true-bypass relay because it utilizes a quieter and smoother switch that is more reliable than traditional bypass switches. Your original tone/signal will remain unaffected when the pedal is not engaged. The cataPulp can provide you with everything from pristine cleans to the edgy, aggressive, grittier side of British distortion. It's time to stand back and let your tone do the fighting. sources.excerpt: Wampler Pedals Unveils the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost: Dual-Channel Overdrive Innovation Meets Studio-Grade Circuit Refinement | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Wampler Pedals Unveils the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost: Dual-Channel Overdrive Innovation Meets Studio-Grade Circuit Refinement By Liam Carter July 13, 2026 Two New Overdrives, One Unified Vision Wampler Pedals has officially launched the Catapulp OD Distortion and Tumnus OD Boost—two distinct yet complementary overdrive pedals designed to address nuanced tonal demands across modern guitar rigs. Announced on March 12, 2024, at the NAMM Show in Anaheim, both units ship with Wampler’s signature powder-coated aluminum enclosures, LED-lit footswitches with status indicators, and internal voltage regulation ensuring consistent performance from 9V to 18V DC. Unlike many boutique manufacturers releasing single-unit updates, Wampler intentionally developed these pedals as a coordinated pair: the Catapulp targets players seeking saturated, harmonically rich distortion with dynamic touch sensitivity, while the Tumnus OD Boost serves as a transparent, articulate boost/overdrive optimized for pedalboard stacking and amp interaction. Both units measure 4.5" × 3.75" × 1.75" and weigh 1.2 lbs—identical dimensions enabling seamless integration into existing pedalboards without footprint compromise. Engineering Philosophy: Beyond Clipping Diodes Wampler’s design team, led by co-founder Brian Wampler and lead engineer Chris Doss, spent 14 months refining analog signal paths that prioritize harmonic integrity over brute-force saturation. Rather than relying solely on silicon or germanium diode clipping, both pedals implement hybrid clipping topologies. The Catapulp uses a cascaded dual-stage architecture: the first stage employs asymmetrical MOSFET-based clipping (IRF510 transistor pair), followed by a second stage using matched 1N5817 Schottky diodes biased at ±0.62V for low-forward-voltage soft clipping. This configuration produces a 22.3dB gain increase at maximum Drive (measured at 1kHz, unity input level) while retaining note definition even at high saturation settings. In contrast, the Tumnus OD Boost utilizes a modified JFET-input buffer stage feeding into a discrete op-amp circuit (Texas Instruments OPA2134PA) before hitting a dynamically biased 1N4148 diode pair—engineered to clip only when transient peaks exceed 1.2Vpp, preserving clean headroom until intentional drive is applied. Power & Signal Integrity Both pedals feature Wampler’s proprietary Clean Power Regulation System (CPRS), which maintains ±0.05V stability across the 9–18V input range. Internal DC-DC conversion isolates the analog path from ripple noise, resulting in measured noise floors of ≤−87.2dBV (A-weighted) at unity gain—verified using Audio Precision APx555 test equipment. Independent bench testing confirmed no measurable difference in THD+N (Total Harmonic Distortion plus Noise) between 9V and 18V operation: 0.08% at 1kHz, 0dBu input, for both units. This eliminates the common 'more voltage = more output' myth; instead, higher voltages expand dynamic headroom and transient response without altering core voicing. The Catapulp OD Distortion: Saturated Texture with Surgical Control The Catapulp OD Distortion distinguishes itself through three dedicated controls—Drive, Tone, and Volume—and an innovative Voice toggle switch offering two distinct clipping voicings. In ‘Vintage’ mode, the circuit emphasizes midrange warmth (peaking at 720Hz ±15Hz) with subtle compression and a smooth high-end roll-off beginning at 5.1kHz. In ‘Modern’ mode, the clipping network shifts bias points to deliver tighter low-end response (−1.8dB at 85Hz), extended treble presence (+2.3dB at 8.4kHz), and 38% faster attack envelope (measured via 10–90% rise time: 1.7ms vs. 2.7ms in Vintage).
